summary: The manuscript presents a 4-page constructive Lean 4.35.0 formalization (18 zero-sorry, zero-Classical.choice theorems) and a pure-Q/Z exact-rational certificate verifier (REV-TRADEOFF-CERT-1.0, 16 canonical certificates, 60-attack red-team suite) auditing the deterministic algebraic, convexity, continuity, separation, chi^2-divergence, and exponent-conservation pillars of Jin, Tang, Wang, and Zhang [4] (arXiv:2611.31982). All fully stated algebraic identities, C^1 spline calculations, Bernstein cancellations, harmonic sums, and Table 2 exact-rational witnesses are internally consistent and verify cleanly, and the exclusion of probabilistic/measure-theoretic proofs is transparently scoped. Minor presentation defects remain: Figure 1(a) mixes inconsistent Pareto frontier conventions across valuation families, Table 1 omits antecedent hypotheses in a few abbreviated theorem rows, and the underlying Lean/Python source code is external to the PDF.
weaknesses: Several Table 1 theorems (#11, #13, #14, #17) reduce to elementary integer arithmetic or constant definitions (e.g., 400 <= 900, 15*10^4 = A, (2-c)+(2+c)=4), limiting the formalization's depth relative to the full sample/query complexity theorems of [4].

Table 1 compresses several theorem statements (#2, #7, #8, #10) to the point where key antecedent hypotheses are omitted from the printed implication, preventing a reader of the PDF alone from checking their exact formal signatures.

Figure 1(a) uses an inconsistent visual convention between MHR/Quasi-MHR (upper-right feasible corner) and Regular/Quasi-Regular (horizontal boundary at beta=3 for alpha <= 3), creating a misleading visual crossing at alpha < 1.5.
Neither the Lean 4 proofs nor the Python verifier code appears in the PDF, so external artifact compilation and replay cannot be audited from the manuscript alone.
